_comment: Trust policy for magik-deploy-role (the role cd.yml assumes via GitHub OIDC).
ALL THREE sub patterns are required, and the reason is the single most common
GitHub-OIDC failure mode:
* cd.yml's `promote-production` job declares `environment: production`.
The MOMENT a job references a GitHub Environment, the OIDC subject claim
changes format to `repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:<name>` — it NO
LONGER carries the ref. A trust policy matching only `ref:refs/tags/*`
therefore rejects it with 'Not authorized to perform
sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity', which is exactly what happened on CD
* cd.yml's `deploy-staging` job declares `environment: staging` for the
same reason (staging gate, added alongside this comment) — same failure
mode, same fix: its own explicit `environment:staging` sub pattern.
* the `ref:refs/tags/*` pattern is kept so any future job in this workflow
that does NOT use an environment still works.
All three remain tightly scoped to this one repository — a fork, another
repo, or a branch push cannot assume this role.
NOTE: this file documents the intended trust policy; applying it to the
real IAM role in AWS (e.g. `aws iam update-assume-role-policy`) is a
separate, manual step — see docs/runbooks/ci-cd.md 'Staging gate'
prerequisites.
WHY EACH SUB IS LISTED TWICE (2026-08-07) — GitHub ID-QUALIFIED SUBJECTS:
GitHub migrated this repository to IMMUTABLE (ID-qualified) OIDC subject
claims. The `sub` now embeds the numeric owner and repo IDs:
repo:vjkarthik98@218363746/MULTIMODAL-...-ASSISTANT@1180642349:environment:staging
instead of the plain `repo:<owner>/<repo>:...` form. Verify the current
format any time with:
gh api repos/vjkarthik98/MULTIMODAL-AGENTIC-RAG-INTEGRATED-KNOWLEDGE-AI-ASSISTANT/actions/oidc/customization/sub
whose `sub_claim_prefix` field is authoritative for what is actually
emitted (the IDs also match `gh api repos/<r> --jq .id` and
`gh api users/<owner> --jq .id`).
This is NOT a config choice we made and NOT something visible from IAM —
the change happened on GitHub's side, under an unchanged trust policy,
between 2026-08-03 (v0.29.0's `deploy` job assumed this role successfully
with `environment: production`) and 2026-08-07 (v0.30.0's `deploy-staging`
failed with 'Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity').
The legacy-form patterns had gone stale without a single local edit, which
is why the policy kept LOOKING correct while denying every request.
BOTH forms are kept deliberately: the ID-qualified ones are what works
today, the legacy ones cost nothing and keep this role working if a run
is ever issued a pre-migration token. Both stay pinned to this one repo —
numeric IDs are globally unique and cannot be re-registered, so the
ID-qualified form is in fact the STRICTER of the two (a deleted-and-
recreated repo of the same name would not match it).
UPDATED 2026-08-21: rebuilt in a NEW AWS account (857194222592, was
537557168406) after the prior account's EC2 instances + EBS volumes were
deleted. THIS FILE IS NOW HISTORICAL/NARRATIVE ONLY -- the actual applied
trust policy is deploy/aws/terraform/iam.tf's
data.aws_iam_policy_document.deploy_role_trust, which builds the same six
sub patterns against a freshly created aws_iam_openid_connect_provider in
the new account. The owner/repo numeric IDs (218363746 / 1180642349) are
unchanged -- they're GitHub-side identifiers, not AWS-side, and survive an
AWS account change untouched.
